original.description: The Copernicus Sentinel-2 Next Generation space component, which is the subject of this procurement, will ensure a seamless continuation of the current Sentinel-2 first generation capabilities, whilst increasing both the quantity and quality of the products. The development of the Sentinel-2 Next Generation (Sentinel-2 NG) Space Component aims to build upon and enhance the initial observations provided by the first generation. In particular, Sentinel-2 NG (S2NG) will respond to the needs of Copernicus Services, with particular emphasis to the Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and the Emergency Management Service (CEMS), together with, as secondary objective, the Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties,  together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include:  - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at: - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_business - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/How_to_do/esa-star_Registration_Process Please note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Full" registration.

original.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

original.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of resilient PNT payload technologies based on digital and AI-enabled architectures. The study will investigate reconfigurable, software-defined payloads capable of characterizing and adapting to dynamic, congested or impaired RF environments.The activity will address the full signal chain, from generation to transmission, including onboard processing and AI-based techniques. A digital twin environment is also foreseen to be developed to support validation andperformance assessment.The objective is to mature concept and associated key payload technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible, flight-representative architecture for next-generation PNT systems.
